To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the electrical properties of ion conducting polymer films are well explained by equations valid for electrolyte solutions; in particular the Onsager model, applied to the parameters of the polymer film, satisfactorily fits the change of the resistance of the polymer film as a function of the relative humidity.

(i) the ion transport mechanism of conducting polymers is the same as that of ionic electrolytes and, therefore, the electrical properties of these polymers can be described by the same theoretical model, and (ii) the Onsager theory, which was developed for ionic electrolytes, is applicable to ion conducting polymers.

1) the change in the electrical conductivity of ion conducting polymers as a function of the relative humidity can be described by the Onsager relation, 2) the Onsager coefficient is related to the diffusion coefficient of the ions in the polymer, 3) the diffusion coefficient can be determined experimentally, 4) the diffusion coefficient of ions in the polymer depends strongly on the nature of the ion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of ion transport in conducting polymer films and with the investigation of the mechanism of the ion transport in such systems.
the study of the transport mechanism in ion-conducting polymer films by the analysis of the electrical properties as a function of the relative humidity.
the study of the transport properties of ion-conducting polymer films and their dependence on environmental parameters, with the aim of understanding the ion transport mechanisms in these materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the electrical transport properties of ion-conducting polymer films can be described by a mechanism similar to that occurring in ionic liquids.
the ion transport in the conducting polymer films occurs via an electrolytic solution mechanism, and that the ion transport is controlled by the water molecules present in the polymer matrix.
the ion transport in the polymer films is governed by the same mechanisms which govern ion transport in electrolytes, but with different characteristic parameters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ion transport mechanism is the same in both electrolytic solutions and ion-conducting polymer films.
the ion transport in these polymer films occurs via the Grotthus mechanism.
the ion transport mechanism is the same for electrolytic solutions and ion-conducting films.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the electrical properties of ion-conducting polymer films are determined by the same mechanisms that govern the electrical properties of electrolytic solutions.
the ion transport mechanism is the same as in electrolytic solutions, and the ion conductivity is controlled by the diffusion and migration processes.
, for a certain class of polymers, the ion transport mechanism can be described in terms of a solution of ions in a solvent, as it is the case for electrolytes.
